backup.archives.empty: No archives yet. If you have just turned backups on, the first one arrives within a minute.
backup.archives.note: Download one now and then and keep it off the NAS. They are encrypted: you can put them anywhere.
backup.archives.restore: Restoring is not done from here, on purpose: you need it exactly when this page no longer opens. It is done from the terminal, with an archive and the private key — see the installation guide.
backup.archives.title: Archives
backup.beside_data: The archives are on the same disk as the data: they protect against a mistake and a failed update, not against the disk breaking or the NAS being stolen. Download one now and then from the list below and keep it elsewhere.
backup.done.generate: Key pair generated. Keep the private key off this NAS, then press Save.
backup.done.run: Backup written. You'll find it in the list below.
backup.done.save: Saved. Automatic backups use these settings.
backup.env_only: These settings come from the container's environment variables: you can see them here, not change them.
backup.frequency.title: Frequency
backup.interval.label: Hours between one backup and the next
backup.keep.label: How many archives to keep
backup.key.change_warning: A new key does not open the archives already written. Generate one only if you have lost the private one, or want to start again from zero.
backup.key.note: Set. Only needed if you want to change it — a new key does not open the old archives.
backup.key.private: This is the private key. It appears only once: without it nobody can reopen your backups. Put it in a password manager, or print it — off this NAS. Then press Save.
backup.key.public_hint: Only this half lives on the instance. It starts with age1…
backup.key.title: Encryption key
backup.not_working: Backups are set up but are not working. Until this is fixed, this instance has nothing to go back to.
backup.setup.intro: You need a key pair: the instance keeps only the public key and writes archives it cannot read back. You see the private key only once — keep it off this NAS.
backup.setup.title: Turn on backups
backup.status.title: Status
invites.done.approved: {{name}} is now part of this instance.
invites.done.created: Invite created. The link to send appears only once: copy it now.
invites.done.rejected: Request refused: the person does not join, and the invite stays as it was.
invites.done.revoked: Invite withdrawn: from now on that link no longer lets anyone ask to join.
invites.error: That didn't work. Try again, now or later.
invites.list.title: Invites created
invites.new.intro: The link works until it expires or is used up, and you can withdraw it whenever you want. Whoever receives it does not join: they ask to join, and the request comes back up here.
invites.new.label: Who is this invite for?
invites.new.label_hint: To remind you who you gave it to. Only you see it.
invites.new.reusable_note: A single-use invite is safer: if it gets passed from hand to hand, you need a new one each time.
invites.new.title: A new invite
invites.requests.empty: Nobody is waiting right now. Whoever opens an invite chooses a name and asks to join: the request appears here, because an invite does not let anyone in on its own — you open the door.
invites.requests.note: An invite does not let anyone in on its own: you decide here who joins.
invites.requests.title: Who asked to join
log.empty.body: What gets decided ends up here: who joins, and which invites are born and die.
log.empty.title: Nothing to show yet
status.at_rest.mismatch: The configuration declares an encryption that the instance does not detect. Until this is cleared up, consider the data not protected if the NAS is stolen.
status.at_rest.title: Encryption at rest
status.connections.note: The instance counts kinds of network, not addresses: whether from outside or inside is the administrator's business; from which address is nobody's business.
status.connections.origin.overlay: from outside, through the private network
status.connections.public_alert: Someone arrived from an address outside the home network and outside the private network. There are two explanations: either a port on the router is open towards the NAS — and then the instance is on the Internet, where it should not be — or there is a proxy between you and it that hides the caller's address. It is worth finding out which.
status.connections.title: Where connections come from
status.data.alert_anonymous: This data will be lost if you update from the panel. It lives on a volume that Docker created by itself, without anyone asking: Docker only carries it over when docker compose recreates the container. The NAS's “update” button, Portainer and Watchtower attach a new, empty one instead, and the instance starts again from zero — accounts, content, photos and the private key, which cannot be replaced. The old data is not deleted: it stays in an orphaned volume, and can be recovered.
status.data.alert_ephemeral: Your data will disappear at the next update. It is not on a volume: it lives inside the container, which is thrown away and rebuilt every time you update the image. Accounts, content, photos and the instance's private key, which cannot be replaced, all go with it.
status.data.title: Where the data lives
status.directory.note: The filesystem refused to tighten it to 0700: other users of this machine can list what is inside. This happens on network shares and on some bind mounts.
status.directory.title: Data folder permissions
status.schema.no_backup_now_configured: This update was applied without a backup first. Migrations only go forward: it has no restore point, and cannot get one later. Backups are now configured — the next update will have one.
status.schema.title: Last schema update
status.schema.versions: Version {{from}} → {{to}}, on {{when}}. This is about that update only, not about today's backups.
status.updates.command_note: Copy this command and run it in the terminal of the NAS or server: it downloads the new image, recognises the configuration and restarts the instance, keeping your data.
status.updates.intro: Check whether a newer version of ESTIA is available. To update the instance, run the command {{command}} in the terminal of the machine or the NAS. Before updating, make sure backups are on.
status.updates.manual_steps: Don't have the “estia” command? Show the manual Docker steps
status.updates.title: Updates
